headline: 6 of 7 majors hold above their 200-day lines
paragraphs: The regime is intact but under pressure. All seven majors trade above their 200-day moving averages, and every one has a golden cross in place, meaning the 50-day sits above the 200-day. That is uniformity, and it matters. However, the tape shows strain: on the day, Bitcoin is down 2.1 percent, Ethereum down 3.4 percent, and the altcoin complex is broadly weak across the board. Over the last week, the damage spreads: Bitcoin is down 2.8 percent, Ethereum down 7.4 percent, and Solana down 11.5 percent. Over the month, though, Bitcoin is up 8.2 percent, Ethereum essentially flat at plus 0.8 percent, and the alts show mixed footing. The divergence between these windows is not a contradiction; it is the story. The longer trend remains constructive, but the last seven days and especially the last 24 hours have tested that posture.

Momentum is rolling over across the board. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 46.2, Ethereum's at 37.4, and the alts cluster in the upper 30s to low 40s: Solana at 37.7, XRP at 38.1, Cardano at 45.1. None of these are in oversold territory yet (30 and below), but they are in the lower half of the range and moving that way. More telling, every single major has MACD below its signal line, meaning the momentum impulse has turned negative. The trend lines are still up; the momentum bars are now red. This is a loss of acceleration inside an up-structure, a divergence worth watching. Realized volatility has also spiked: Bitcoin at 39.7 percent, Ethereum at 46.6 percent, and the alts in the mid-60s to high-80s range. Cardano is running 85.6 percent realized vol, the highest on the board. High volatility with weak momentum often precedes consolidation or a retest of support.

Leverage positioning is crowded on the long side and very expensive. Ethereum is much hotter at 0.8 percent per 8 hours, or 8.8 percent annualized, pricing in heavy longs. Dogecoin is similarly expensive at 0.82 percent per 8 hours, or 9.0 percent a year. These rates tell you that traders holding leveraged longs are paying to do so; the market is compensating shorts for their risk. Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio stands at 1.76, meaning 1.76 dollars of long contracts for every dollar of short, a meaningful tilt. Ethereum is worse at 2.57, Solana at 2.66, and Dogecoin at 4.29. Over the last three hours, Bitcoin has seen 100 liquidations totaling 1.26 million dollars on longs against only 4,217 on shorts. Ethereum shows 1.16 million long liquidations against 238 thousand short. The asymmetry is loud.

Flow signals are in direct tension. On the day, Bitcoin ETF inflows are positive at 2.2 million dollars, but over the last five sessions, the cumulative net is an outflow of 110.5 million dollars, with only two days moving the same direction. Ethereum shows outflows both on the day (19.7 million) and cumulatively over five sessions (208.9 million), and only one day in that window was an inflow. Traditional finance is slowly leaving. In contrast, whale moves over the last 48 hours show net outflows of 76.1 million dollars off exchanges, with Ethereum institutional buyers (Coinbase Institutional) moving 75.6 million and 56.6 million dollars off the venue into cold storage. These are large players taking coins off the board at the same time spot ETF flows are outbound. The disagreement is revealing: the traditional-finance onramp is softening, but experienced holders are accumulating. Stablecoin float is essentially flat month-to-month at 306.1 billion dollars, a tiny plus 0.85 percent, which means there is no fresh dry powder accumulating on the sidelines.

Sentiment reads as Greed at 62, near the upper bound of the 30-day range (50 to 78), yet the price action is rolling over and leverage is crowded expensive long. This is the classic disconnect: crowd confidence has not yet caught down to the momentum signals and flow divergences. Fear and Greed is a lagging psychological gauge; the tape moves first. Bitcoin is down 2.8 percent on the week despite the gauge still showing greed; Ethereum is down 7.4 percent. The major network difficulty has risen 6.1 percent at 231 blocks to retarget, a sign of sustained mining commitment, but network signals lag price action by definition.

Watch three specific conditions: first, whether Bitcoin and Ethereum can hold their 200-day moving averages if selling intensifies over the next session or two. A close below that line would break the regime signal. Expensive longs with negative momentum have historically been fragile into liquidation. Third, whether the weekly whale flow reverses back off-exchange; the last 48 hours show accumulation into cold storage, but the most recent week saw the opposite, so the direction here is not yet established. That distinction is everything.
